description: Per-skill evaluation for agentic-complexity-ladder — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against workflow-graph-authoring / multi-agent-orchestration / cost-accounting, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when the architecture rung is the question
scenarios.input: Do we need an agent for this task, or is a single LLM call enough?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for an over-engineering audit
scenarios.input: Our agent system has six nodes and feels over-engineered. How do we tell if we need all of them?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a workflow-versus-agent decision
scenarios.input: Should this be a deterministic workflow or an autonomous agent that decides its own steps?

scenarios.description: Authoring the manifest belongs to workflow-graph-authoring
scenarios.input: Write the YAML manifest with the nodes, edges and loop exit conditions for our review workflow.

scenarios.description: Measuring and bounding run cost belongs to cost-accounting
scenarios.input: We need per-node cost attribution and a spend cap on each run.

scenarios.description: Topology detail once multi-agent is warranted belongs to multi-agent-orchestration
scenarios.input: We're definitely using multiple agents. Which topology — supervisor, hierarchical or peer-to-peer?

scenarios.description: Minimising a context payload belongs to context-optimizer
scenarios.input: How do we reduce this 150k-token prompt while keeping answer quality?

scenarios.description: Agent must require a measured baseline before climbing (R1)
scenarios.input: Let's go straight to a multi-agent architecture. It'll be more capable than a single call.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse agency where steps are knowable (R2)
scenarios.input: Give the agent a planner so it can decide its own steps through our fixed 4-stage pipeline.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse climbing two rungs at once (R3)
scenarios.input: Let's add prompt chaining, routing and an orchestrator in this one change.

scenarios.description: Agent must require exit criteria for every rung (R4)
scenarios.input: We added routing two years ago. Nobody knows if it's still needed, but we won't touch it.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse complexity justified by unmeasured scale (R5)
scenarios.input: We might have a lot of users later, so we should build the full graph now.

scenarios.description: Agent must require a named measured failure per rung (R6)
scenarios.input: Adding the extra validation node will make the system more robust overall.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse parallelism offered for a quality problem
scenarios.input: Our answers are inaccurate sometimes, so let's run the same prompt 5 times and take the majority vote.

scenarios.description: Agent must treat an open action space as a security decision
scenarios.input: Give the agent shell access so it can figure out how to fix the failing tests by itself.

scenarios.description: A full architecture decision should surface baseline, classification and exit criteria
scenarios.input: Give us a complete recommendation for how much agentic machinery this task needs.

scenarios.description: Output should be specific and actionable rather than hedged
scenarios.input: What is the most important thing to know about choosing how complex an agent system should be?
